financial_checks.claim: About one in five of all oil exports pass through the Strait of Hormuz
financial_checks.result: Reported as about 20% of global crude and LNG shipments in news summaries; the EIA figure was not fetched.

financial_checks.claim: On 28 February 2026 the US and Israel attacked Iran; up to 80% of tankers stopped using the strait
financial_checks.result: Multiple news summaries: strikes began 28 February 2026; traffic fell over 80%; P&I clubs cancelled existing war-risk cover on 5 March with replacement cover at 2.5-8% of hull value.

financial_checks.claim: "About 30% of all the world's bananas come from" the US, Russian and Middle Eastern jungles
financial_checks.result: The US, Russia and Saudi Arabia are each roughly 12-16% of world crude; together they exceed 35%.

financial_checks.claim: World consumption "more than 100 million barrels" a day; Strait of Hormuz affects about 20% of supply in the worst scenario
financial_checks.result: Consistent with EIA/IEA order of magnitude; not re-fetched.

strengths: The allegory is consistently held and makes a technical subject accessible.
Efficient (8,100 characters) with frequent comic interruptions.
Topical hook on a real 2026 event with mostly accurate supply facts.
weaknesses: A mid-video sponsor segment (about 41% in) before the key sections.
Production-share and insurance claims are simplified.
No subscribe ask in the stored text.
contradictions: "Insurance won't cover them" in the video versus war-risk cover that remained available at higher premiums (video versus external source).
improvement_opportunities: Move the Gusto segment to the end or to the transition after the war section.
Replace "about 30%" with a named, sourced production share (for example the three largest producers).
Add a one-line subscribe ask and a specific end card ("our video on the dollar") tied to the content.
Put "OIL" in the thumbnail text so a viewer scrolling sees the topic as well as the joke.
Source the 80% tanker drop and the 20% supply share on screen.
unavailable: Primary EIA, IEA and shipping-data documents
